extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, impressionists, and performers learning mimicry/comedic impressions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for performing comedic impressions (imitating celebrity/cartoon voices and mannerisms), covering vocal and physical techniques, persona, comedic framing, difficulty levels, and a short performance rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal mimicry
rubrics_metrics.description: A performer matches the target's voice by reproducing pitch, cadence, accent, distinctive phrases/catchphrases, and speech rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key techniques: voice match (pitch, cadence, accent); distinctive phrases / catchphrases; speech rhythm. Level note: 'voice only' impressions are easier and podcast-friendly. Success judged by how well the listener recognizes the target from voice alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical mimicry
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducing the target's gestures, posture, facial expressions, walking gait, and idiosyncratic movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key techniques: gestures and posture, facial expressions, walking gait, idiosyncratic movements. Performance medium: adding face/body increases difficulty (on-camera or live). Use physical elements to amplify or punctuate vocal imitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude / persona (the mind behind the speech)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conveying the target's internal attitude, swagger, and characteristic mindset — what that person would think and say, especially placed into new contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques: 'get the swagger', inhabit the mind behind the speech, and imagine what the person would say in a NEW context. Persona work differentiates mere mimicry from a living, improv-capable character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurd-context juxtaposition (comedic framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Putting the celebrity/character into absurd or unexpected contexts (the 'what if X said Y' engine) to generate comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Why it's funny: recognition pleasure plus surprise when a familiar voice is saying something out-of-context. Use juxtaposition to serve jokes rather than only to reproduce the target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizability (voice-only recognizability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the voice is recognizable on hearing only, without visual cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric question: 'Is the voice recognizable on hearing only?' This is a core evaluative measure, especially important for audio mediums (podcast/radio).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture of physical mannerisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the performer's physical mannerisms match the target's characteristic movements and expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric question: 'Are physical mannerisms captured?' This assesses the physical fidelity of the impression for on-camera or live performances; overlaps with 'Physical mimicry' but frames it as an evaluative check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealing something true about the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The impression should surface or articulate an observed truth about the target that audiences recognize but may not have put into words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Why it's funny: the mimic captures something everyone has noticed but nobody can articulate. The page notes 'Best impressions REVEAL something true about the subject.' Use choice of trait or exaggeration to make that truth evident and comedic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impression in service of a joke (not just imitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The impression should be used to deliver or enhance a joke rather than merely imitate the target as a tribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic use vs. pure imitation: pure imitation is a tribute act; comedic impressions place the impression in service of a joke. Explicit rubric question: 'Is the impression in service of a joke (not just imitation)?' Anti-pattern: accurate but purposeless mimicry that lacks comedic intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to improvise in character
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the performer can spontaneously speak/act as the character in new, unscripted situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric question: 'Could the mimic improvise in the character's voice?' Level note: 'Improvised in character' is the master level of difficulty. Improvisation demonstrates deep persona understanding and keeps performances fresh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levels of difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: A four-tiered classification of impression complexity: (1) voice only, (2) voice + face, (3) voice + face + body, (4) improvised in character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level details: 1) Voice only — easiest; podcast-friendly. 2) Voice + face — harder; suitable for on-camera. 3) Voice + face + body — hardest; best for live performance. 4) Improvised in character — master level. Use these levels to set expectations, judge technical demands, and choose appropriate mediums for a given impression.
